observed.text:
The problem
    Every release is the same six steps, done by hand, at the worst possible hour.
    They are not hard steps. They are steps that must all happen, in order,
      without one being forgotten. That is a machine's job, and it has been a person's job
      for a decade.
    
      
        Before
        
          Tag the version
          Write the changelog
          Run the build
          Sign the artifact
          Publish to the registry
          Announce in the channel
        
      
      
        After
        
          Tag the version
          Write the changelog
          Run the build
          Sign the artifact
          Publish to the registry
          cadence ship

Measured
    What the collapse actually saved.
    Numbers from the Cadence team's own releases over one quarter. This is a
      fictional product built as a DesignOS golden, so these are illustrative, not audited.
    
      
        Median release time
        4m 12s
        Down from 38 minutes of hands-on work spread across an afternoon.
      
      
        Steps a human performs
        1
        The command. Everything after it is the machine's responsibility.
      
      
        Releases missing a changelog
        0
